name: Activity recognition
plain: Asks to detect walking, driving, cycling and step counts.
meaning: Motion classes reveal commutes, exercise habits and sleep schedules. On both OSes it is gated by a runtime prompt.

android.note: Needed for step counter and detector sensors starting with Android 10 (API 29).

ios.note: Raw accelerometer and gyroscope reads do not need a prompt on iOS.

data.update: event driven; step counts per interval

limits.headline: Can tell if you walk, drive or cycle, and count steps, after you allow Motion
limits.user_action: You tap Allow when the app asks for physical activity or motion access
can: Detect walking, running, cycling and driving
Look back about 7 days of activity on iPhone
Wake in the background through Play services on Android
cannot: Record activity before you allow it
Keep going if you turn the permission off in Settings
Skip the prompt on Android 10 and newer for step counters (iPhone raw motion sensors need no prompt)
limits.differs: Android 10 and newer needs Activity recognition permission for step sensors. iPhone asks for Motion and Fitness.

story.what_it_is: An app asks to know if you are walking, running, cycling or in a vehicle, and to count steps.

marketing.name: Activity recognition
marketing.pitch: Android can detect when you walk, run or ride so apps can respond to what you are doing.

marketing.name: Motion and Fitness
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps show your steps, distance and activity type when you allow Motion and Fitness.

story.for_you: You see a prompt asking to access physical activity or Motion and Fitness. If you allow it, the app can show your steps and know when you start a run or ride. If you say no, some tracking features do not work.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to start workouts on their own, count steps cheaply and know when you are driving so they do not bother you. It also builds a picture of your daily routine: commute, exercise and sleep times.

use_cases.example: A running app starts recording the moment it senses you running, so you never forget to press start.
A walking game turns your real steps into hatching eggs and rewards.
A step counter shows daily steps and a weekly streak.
A driving score app detects that you are in a car and starts to log the trip.
A map app switches to walking directions once it sees you step out of a car.
An insurance or ad partner reads how much you move to guess your health.

story.android_note: Android asks for the Physical activity permission, and an app can get walking, driving and step events.
story.ios_note: iPhone calls this Motion and Fitness. Apps ask once, and you can turn it off in Settings.

technical_bounds: Raw motion sensors need no prompt
Step count history limited to 7 days on iOS

history.change: M7 motion coprocessor introduced; motion access via CoreMotion
